Class EventRouter

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.toolkit.event.EventRouter
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class EventRouter extends Object implements AutoCloseable
Routes events to elements based on focus and position.

Events are routed as follows:

  • Key events go to the focused element
  • Mouse events go to the element at the mouse position
  • Tab/Shift+Tab navigate focus
  • Drag events are tracked and routed to the dragged element

Events can be consumed by handlers to stop propagation.

The router uses an ElementRegistry to track element areas by ID, which can be used by external systems (like effects) to look up element positions.

Event routing decisions can be traced via JFR events (when enabled).

      Parameters:

    • addGlobalHandler

      public void addGlobalHandler(ActionHandler handler)
      Adds an action handler as a global event handler.

      This is a convenience method that wraps the action handler. Events are dispatched to the action handler before reaching elements.

      Parameters:
      handler - the action handler to add

    • removeGlobalHandler

      public void removeGlobalHandler(GlobalEventHandler handler)
      Removes a global event handler.
      Parameters:
      handler - the handler to remove

    • registerElement

      public void registerElement(Element element, Rect area)
      Registers an element for event routing. Called during rendering to build the element list. The area is stored internally - elements don't need to track it.

      If an element is already registered, this updates its area but does not add a duplicate entry.

      Elements are also registered in the ElementRegistry for CSS-like queries by external systems (like effects).

      Parameters:
      element - the element to register
      area - the element's rendered area

    • clear

      public void clear()
      Clears all registered elements. Should be called at the start of each render cycle.

    • route

      public EventResult route(Event event)
      Routes an event to the appropriate element(s).

      For key events, the focused element is given first chance to handle the event. This allows text inputs to consume character keys before global handlers see them. Global handlers are called after element routing if the event wasn't handled.

      Parameters:
      event - the event to route
      Returns:
      HANDLED if any handler handled the event, UNHANDLED otherwise
